## During the seminar

A tea-tasting experiment introduces null distributions and p-values.
We connect rejection rules to Type I and Type II errors, relate tests to
confidence intervals, and compare one-sample, independent two-sample,
and paired tests. A paired test is a one-sample test of within-person differences.

Power calculations show how sample size, effect size, variability, and the
significance level affect the chance of detecting a difference. We finish with
resampling: bootstrapping approximates a sampling distribution, while
randomization tests reproduce the assignment mechanism under a null hypothesis.
A simulated household experiment shows why the resampling unit matters.
